children: Alphabet, the Google parent and cloud-services group

, launched Gemini 4 Argon to developers, businesses and paid subscribers, while its Class A shares traded at $353.10, down approximately 0.20%, at 10.20 am EST on October 14. The investor question is straightforward: how much paying demand can Google build before its introductory API rates expire on November 30? Broad access gives the model a large potential audience. Turning that reach into repeat spending is the next hurdle.

Google's launch announcement puts introductory API pricing at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. After November 30, those rates double to $4 and $20. Developers and enterprises can access Argon through AI Studio and Google's Gemini platform. Pro and Ultra subscribers get access in the Gemini app and Search's AI Mode, while Ultra subscribers can also use it in Antigravity. That gives Google several routes to customers, but availability alone does not establish the rollout's revenue contribution.

The pricing change makes retention worth watching. An illustrative workload of one million input tokens and 100,000 output tokens costs $3 initially and $6 afterward, excluding caching discounts and other adjustments. Will customers keep spending when the discount disappears? The valuation chart adds pressure: the $353.10 share price sits 36.97% above the $257.79 GF Value estimate, suggesting investors already price in substantial growth. Argon's commercial test is whether trial usage becomes durable paid demandand whether that demand translates into meaningful earnings.

title: Alphabet Stocks Trade 36.97% Above GF Value as Google Launches Gemini 4 Argon
